summary: Iteration 22 — verified both backend security fixes on top of iter 21. All 7 pytest tests PASS (7/7, 100%). (1) Rate-limiter now honours X-Forwarded-For: 7 rapid POSTs with X-Forwarded-For: 10.10.10.101 → first 5 return 201, attempts 6–7 return 429. Fresh IP 10.10.10.202 immediately gets a clean quota (3/3 → 201). (2) BodySizeLimitMiddleware works: 50k-char message (Content-Length > 32 KB) with X-Forwarded-For: 10.10.10.203 → HTTP 413 with exactly {"detail": "Request body too large."}. Regressions all green: normal 500-char POST → 201 with exactly {id, email_sent}; GET /api/enquiries → 405; GET /api/health → 200 with all 5 security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security); /sitemap.xml still contains /privacy-policy/, /cookie-policy/, /terms-of-use/. Frontend re-run skipped per main-agent instruction (iter 21 was 100% green and no backend fix touched frontend surface).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _client_ip(): correct precedence (XFF → X-Real-IP → remote_address) and left-most token parsing. Consider adding `forwarded-allow-ips` scoping if uvicorn ever gets --proxy-headers, but for slowapi-only key-func this is fine.

server.py BodySizeLimitMiddleware: only checks Content-Length header. A malicious client omitting Content-Length and using chunked transfer encoding could bypass this. Low risk because the ingress typically injects Content-Length; still worth a note for defence-in-depth (could stream and count bytes, or set `client_max_body_size` at the ingress).

Middleware order: BodySizeLimitMiddleware is added AFTER SecurityHeadersMiddleware in code, which (due to Starlette's LIFO middleware stack) means the size check runs FIRST (outermost) — this is the correct ordering, oversized requests are rejected before hitting any downstream handler. Verified working.
413 response bypasses SecurityHeadersMiddleware because it's returned from the outermost middleware. Not a functional bug; noted for completeness.
